appraisal_events.evidence: The duc treats all his tenants as 'fermiers, manants, acquéreurs de biens nationaux, dont l'opinion ne compte pas,' calls Jupien's demand for indemnity 'une infamie de la part de ce quidam,' and mockingly threatens him with 'bientôt ce particulier vous appellera citoyen Norpois' — yet when he needs a favor from the narrator's father he fusses over his collar and clasps his hand 'avec une impudeur de courtisane,' leading him 'en laisse.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes a contradiction in the duc's character: imperious contempt for those he deems socially beneath him coexists with an obsequious, self-interested fawning toward those whose services he needs, undercutting his grandeur.

status_effects.explanation: The duc's standing in the passage drops sharply as the narrator lays bare his contemptuous entitlement toward Jupien alongside his servile eagerness toward the father when useful to him.
Jupien holds his ground against the duc's outburst, feigning ignorance of the duchess's supposed charity, and comes through the confrontation unintimidated.
